newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sees c/a deficit near $17 bln in yr - Sept.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sees c/a deficit near $17 bln in yr - Sept.

text.p: South Korea's current account deficit in the year to September will be near $17 billion, Yoon Je-cho, senior counsellor to South Korea's Finance Minister said on Thursday.
He added that the government was targetting a 2-3 percent annual rate in the consumer price index (CPI) by the year 2000.
When asked if he agreed with market estimates for a $17 billion current account deficit for the year to September, Cho said "that's close to the mark".
But he said he expected the deficit to improve gradually over 1997.

"Our current account deficit next year will not be worse than this year," he told reporters at a briefing on South Korea's recent invitation to join the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
Cho said South Korea was aiming for price stability similar to that achieved by most OECD members and had already brought inflation steadily down since the early 1990s.
He said he expected annual inflation this year to run at between 4.5 to 5.0 percent, nearly unchanged from 1995.
"We're continuing to put a lot of effort into reducing inflation," Cho said.
